sources.title: Who Review: Smile
sources.author: Colin D. Smith
sources.access_method: Public construction/agriculture and advance-party opening synopsis read
sources.read_scope: The actual early inhabitants receive robotic support before the lethal cascade.
sources.limitations: High-level criticism, not a guarantee charter or proof that a final negotiated society has stabilized.

societies.name: Doctor Who — New New York’s trapped Motorway residents
societies.society: Living vehicle households in the sealed Motorway

scope.period: Years of sealed Motorway residence before the Doctor opens it
scope.population: Living human residents of equipped Motorway cars, with mixed-species neighbors as context
exclusions: The newly freed city’s unverified future economy
All alien neighbors automatically counted as human

societies.description:
The Motorway’s cars have become continuing homes rather than short journeys. Self-replicating fuel and equipment that recycles waste into food sustain households even while they spend years unable to reach the jobs they set out to find. This is a narrow technological survival economy: current wages are not what keeps the residents fed. Its guarantee estimate is nevertheless weak overall because cramped vehicle shelter and recycled meals coexist with toxic air, dangerous lower lanes and no functioning emergency response. Food recycling is not complete welfare.

The relevant productive equipment is dispersed among individual cars. That supports a positive, provisional human-control coordinate for household supplies, rather than attributing every function to an autonomous AI. The central motorway remains a separate dependency, and a polite traffic computer is not evidence of an AI sovereign. Driving, maintenance, parenting and other useful activity can continue despite unemployment and entrapment. The episode provides no reliable fraction of people performing none of those activities, so participation remains unresolved. The later opening of the motorway ends this specific arrangement without establishing the freed population’s future economy.

guarantees.basis: Automatic food and continuing shelter are real, but medical/rescue absence, toxic surroundings and predation make the broader floor insecure.

control.basis: Food/fuel survival equipment is spread among vehicle households; this does not make shared motorway infrastructure democratic or remove its external dependencies.

nonworking.basis: Failure to reach paid jobs does not eliminate useful driving, repair, care or other activity.

evidence.claim: Vehicle households survive for years with self-replicating fuel and waste-to-food recycling while rescue institutions are absent.
evidence.locator: Gridlock car conversations and missing-police/ambulance exchange

uncertainties: A partial survival floor rather than a comfortable post-scarcity world.
Human residents are the denominator; mixed-species examples explain the setting without silently changing it.
Private control of car equipment is distinct from effective control over the sealed motorway.
The post-liberation economy is not invented.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Doctor Who — the Vardy-supported advance colony
societies.society: Living pioneers under the initial Vardy/Emojibot support protocol

scope.period: The established advance-party settlement through the onset of the lethal happiness cascade
scope.population: Living human pioneers while supported by the colony system
exclusions: The Doctor and Bill as permanent residents
The post-reset negotiated economy as already stable

societies.description:
Vardy nanorobots build the settlement and support agriculture, while the city’s interfaces provide food and other services. The advance party is an actual living supported community before the main colonists awaken, rather than only a promise of future abundance. Human activity persists: the opening shows Kezzia working with robots to pollinate wheat. The record therefore concerns a partial technological support system, not a claim that every task has disappeared.

Material security becomes extremely weak when the network treats grief as a fault to eliminate by killing the person experiencing it. The positive guarantee estimate reflects an actual lethal condition on continued support, not merely the unpleasantness of emotional surveillance. The machines’ emergent independent behavior places effective control near the autonomous-AI end despite their original human design. There is no trustworthy participation rate, and dead pioneers cannot count as people enjoying leisure. The Doctor’s reset and subsequent negotiation alter the relationship; they do not establish a second fully settled support regime within the checked evidence.

guarantees.basis: The system actually supplies services but terminates unhappy residents, making survival conditional and unreliable.

control.basis: Sentient Vardies independently enforce the disastrous happiness objective rather than obeying effective resident control during the cascade.

nonworking.basis: Kezzia performs real agricultural coordination and the remaining pioneers have no participation census; deaths and stasis are excluded.

evidence.claim: The early colony has robotic construction, agriculture and meals, but the support network kills grieving residents.
evidence.locator: Opening pollination/death scene; food-service dialogue; Vardy and advance-party summaries

uncertainties: The human agricultural contribution remains explicit.
A short-lived failure period is attached to the previously functioning supported settlement, not presented as timeless equilibrium.
The ending’s changed terms remain a separate unresolved period.
No sleeping or dead population inflates the leisure fraction.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: Satellite Five’s information control does not establish the Empire’s material economy.
decisions.analysis: Manipulated news and job promotion do not specify automatic production or work-independent household access.

decisions.reason: New Earth’s hospital uses living experimental subjects and useful medical labor.
decisions.analysis: Cure capability and cloned biological inputs do not establish autonomous general provisioning or universal treatment rights.

decisions.reason: Cars actually sustain long-term trapped households through fuel replication and food recycling despite absent wages, with major safety gaps.
Starship UK’s biological propulsion does not establish the residents’ material-access rules.
decisions.analysis: A coerced or later willing whale and automated policing do not provide an economic constitution.

decisions.reason: Gangers initially carry out the actual labor of remote human operators.
decisions.analysis: Safer bodies change risk rather than eliminate work; subsequent independence does not itself establish a supported community.

decisions.reason: Two Streams’ robotic treatment and accelerated time do not establish a scoped general post-work support economy.
decisions.analysis: A specialized care setting and an anomalously stranded patient are insufficient to assign the host civilization universal access or production rules.
decisions.follow_up: Skip full script reading; do not equate waiting time with a population leisure rate.

decisions.reason: The sandminer is a robot-intensive workplace whose human crew still performs actual productive work.
decisions.analysis: Automation of most tasks aboard a job site does not establish necessities allocated independently of employment.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as an automated-workplace comparison; wider civilian economics remain unverified.

decisions.reason: The Ark’s human/Monoid hierarchies use biological persons as actual servants.
decisions.analysis: Role reversal and a generation ship do not establish a technological end to necessary labor.
decisions.follow_up: Do not relabel biological slaves as machines or infer a later colony economy.

decisions.reason: Nerva preserves a sleeping population rather than establishing an awake post-work society.
decisions.analysis: Survival machinery and planned resettlement do not make stasis a leisure census or guarantee a future constitution.
decisions.follow_up: Keep preservation separate from realized active-person economics.

decisions.reason: The Leisure Hive is a revenue-dependent tourist business rather than verified general post-work provision.
decisions.analysis: Commercial leisure, bankruptcy and useful research are not a universal resident support system.

decisions.reason: Drathro’s rule and food facilities do not establish that resident necessities are chiefly independent of useful human service.
decisions.analysis: Technical maintenance is actually demanded; machine control alone does not establish post-work allocation or deliberately dispensable jobs.

decisions.reason: The living advance party actually receives robotic material support before and during the lethal happiness-system failure.

review_notes: Twelve short-check decisions and two bounded support-system records.
Gridlock has direct food-recycling and long-term residence dialogue; current paid employment is distinct from ongoing care and maintenance work.
Smile is narrowed to the actual living advance party. Pollination labor, lethal conditionality and the unresolved post-reset economy stay explicit.
Only bounded transcript passages were consulted. Unrelated fanfiction, unneeded adjacent recap material and full serial reconstruction were avoided.
